safety.definition: THE DANGER ZONE: 4–60°C (40–140°F), where pathogens multiply: the two-hour rule governs everything left in it. Cooling law: hot food to 21°C within 2 hours, to 4°C within 4 more (shallow pans, ice baths: never a stockpot straight into the walk-in). CROSS-CONTAMINATION: raw below ready-to-eat in storage, color-coded boards, hands and towels as vectors. FIFO: first in, first out: label and date everything (masking tape and a Sharpie run more restaurants than any software). HACCP is the systematized version: identify hazards, control critical points, document. Allergen protocol is service-critical and legal-critical. None of this is glamour; all of it is the license to do the glamorous parts.

inspections.definition: The visits and the bad days, prepared for in advance. INSPECTIONS: know your jurisdiction's system (letter grades posted in the window, point scores, risk-based frequency), and run the kitchen so ANY moment is inspection-ready: the food-safety entry's disciplines (temps logged, FIFO labeled, hand sinks stocked and USED, sanitizer buckets titrated) aren't inspection prep; they're the daily standard the inspection merely photographs. During the visit: accompany professionally, correct on the spot what can be, never argue, get every finding in writing; after: fix, document, retrain at pre-shift, and treat repeat findings as management failures, not staff ones. CRISIS PLAYBOOKS, written before needed: FOODBORNE-ILLNESS COMPLAINT (take it seriously and kindly, gather specifics, preserve records and product, call the insurer and, if credible, the health department yourself; the cover-up is always worse than the event), equipment catastrophe (the walk-in dies: thermometer logs decide what's saved; the insurance entry's breakdown rider decides what's paid), fire/flood (business interruption's moment), viral bad review or social-media pile-on (respond once, gracefully, factually; never brawl online), and the power outage's food-disposition rules. THE PRINCIPLE: crises are inevitable; scandals are optional: the difference is preparation, documentation, and the instinct to protect guests first, reputation second, and ego never. A binder nobody needed is cheap; the one you needed and didn't have is the whole business.

svHardware.term: Sous Vide Hardware: Circulators, Sealers & Safety Kit
svHardware.definition: The equipment half of the technique wing's sous vide entry. The IMMERSION CIRCULATOR (Anova/Breville-class): a heater-pump clipped to any pot or Cambro: hold ±0.1–0.5°C for hours to days; that's the whole machine, and the affordable ones are genuinely sufficient. SEALING: edge (suction) sealers handle most work (freeze liquids first, or use the water-displacement zip-bag method, legitimate, not cheating); CHAMBER sealers are the pro leap: they seal LIQUIDS (marinades, stocks, compression pickles' instant-infusion party trick) and buy-in-bulk economics. The supporting cast: a lidded 12qt Cambro (evaporation control on long cooks), bag weights/racks (floaters cook unevenly: the one silent failure mode), and the safety literacy: pasteurization is time-AT-temperature tables (thickness matters), the 4.5–54.5°C danger window still applies to lazy cooling, and chill-shock (ice bath) anything held for later. Then the finish: screaming pan, torch, or grill: the circulator cooks; the fire still gets the last word.

fda.name: FDA Food Code 2022
fda.note: United States. Adopted state by state, with amendments and on their own schedule, so the figure your inspector holds you to may differ.

fsa.name: UK Food Standards Agency
fsa.note: England, Wales and Northern Ireland regulations, and FSA cooking guidance. Scotland sets no chilled figure in law.

rows.label: Cold holding
rows.fsa: 8°C or below in law; 5°C or below recommended

rows.label: Cooling cooked food
rows.fda: 135°F (57°C) to 70°F (21°C) within 2 hours, then to 41°F (5°C) within 4 more

rows.label: Poultry, stuffed meats and reheated leftovers
rows.fsa: 75°C, or 70°C held for two minutes: one figure for everything cooked

rows.label: Whole cuts of beef, pork, lamb and fish
Sanitiser strength
rows.fda: chlorine 50 to 100 ppm · quaternary ammonium per the label, commonly 150 to 400 ppm · iodine 12.5 to 25 ppm
